Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

FOREWORD 

Ibis  Indian  Standard  was  adopted  by  the  Bureau  of  Indiaa  Standards  od  20  November  19S9»  after 
the  draft  finalized  by  the  Wool  and  Woof  Products  Sectional  Committee  had  been  approved  by  the 
Textile  DiviBion  Council, 

Wool/polypropylene  blankets  are  being  increasingly  used  within  the  country  due  to  its  several  advao- 
tages  like  lighter  in  weight,  durable  and  sufficiently  warm.  Keeping  these  in  view  the  present  standard 
has  been  formulated.  It  is  hoped  that  the  pubJication  of  this  standard  would  help  in  mannfacturing 
wool/polypropykae  blankets  of  required  quality  and  ensure  the  availability  of  euch  quality  products 
in  the  market. 

For  the  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this  sUndard  is  complied  with,  the 
final  value,  observed  or  calculated^  expressing  the  result  of  a  test  or  analysis^  shall  be  rounded  off  in 
accordance  with  IS  2  :  1960  *  Rules  for  rounding  off  numerical  values  {revised)'.  The  number  of 
significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  off  value  should  be  the  same  as  that  of  the  specified  value 
in  this  standard.

1  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  prescribes  the  construction 
dctai/s  and  other  particulars  for  wool/poJypro- 
p^^lene  blended  blankets. 

1.2  This  standard  does  not  specify  general 
appearance  and  feel  of  the  blankets  (  see  also  4  ). 

2  REFERENCES 

2.1  The  Indian  Standard  Jisted  in  Annex  A  are 
necessary  adjuncts  to  this  standard. 

3  'reRMlNOU>GY 

5.1  For  the  purpose  of  this  standard,  the  defini- 
tions given  in  IS  11206  :  1984  shall  apply. 

4  MANUFACTURE 

4.1  The  parameters  of  wool  and  polypropylene 
fibres  used  for  manufacturing  the  yarn,  method  of 
dyeing  and  the  type  of  tinish  are  as  given  in 
Table  t.  The  approximate  count  of  yarn  is  also 
given  in  Table  1  for  guidance  only, 

4.1.1  The  method  of  dyeing  and  finish  of  blankets 
are  given  in  Table  1 . 

4.2  BUnkefs 

The  blankets  shaf/  be  properfy  washed  and  shall 
be  free  from  grease,  soap,  filling  or  any  other 
admixture  which  might  give  fictitious  mass  or 
firmness. 

4.2,1  Finish 

The  blankets  shaJl  be  milled  and  given  a  raised 
finish. 


4.3.2  Moth  Pro^g 

In  case  the  blankets  arc  to  be  mothproofed,  the 
same  shaH  be  rendered  mothproof  by  suitable 
mothprooOng  chemicals  as  per  IS  1 1662  ;  1986 
which  wJIJ  not  have  toxic  eifect  on  human  body. 
The  manufacturer  shall  declare  the  mothproofing 
chemicals  used,  the  minimum  residual  content  and 
the  method  of  test  for  determining  the  same. 

4.2.2.1  The  amount  of  preservatives  used  in  the 
treatment  of  blankets  shall  be  determined  by  the 
methods  given  in  IS  5522  (  J>art  3  )  :  1983. 

4.2.3  Freedom  from  Defects 

The  blankets  when  visually  examined  on  a  fiat 
surface  shall  not  have  any  objectionable  flaw. 
The  objectionable  flaws  shall  be  those  whkh 
immediately  strike  the  eyes  of  the  person  examin- 
ing the  blankets  and  shall  be  deemed  to  include: 

a>  j^ssJng  ends  and  picks^ 
b>  floats, 

c)  cuts  and  holesr 

d)  stains^ 

e)  weft  bars  and  warp  section  marks,  and 

f )  big  stubs  and  knots. 

4.2.3.1  Reference  tnay  be  m&6t  to  ys  4125  :  19%f 
for  details  of  these  flaws.

shall  be  as  given  in  Table  2.

NOTES 

1  In  case  of  dispute,  colour  fastness  to  light  shall  be 
determined  by  the  method  prescribed  in  IS  686  :  1983. 

2  The  blend  composition  may  be  varied  as  agreetl 
to  between  the  buyer  and  the  seller  subject  to  a 
minimum  of  55  percent  wool  and  maximum  45  per- 
cent of  polypropylene.  The  tolerance  on  blend 
composition  shall  be  ±1  unit  on  the  agreed  per- 
centage. 

6  SEALED  SAMPLES 

6.1  If  in  order  to  illustrate  or  specify  general 
appearance* /eel  shade  etc  of  blankets,  a  sample 
has  been  agreed  upon  and  sealed,  the  supply  shall 
be  in  conformity  with  the  sairkple  in  such  respects- 


fi*l.t  The  custody  of  the  sealed  sample  shall  be 
a  matter  of  prior  agreement  between  (he  bayer 
and  the  seller. 


7  MARKING 

7.1  The  blankets  shall  be  marked  with  the 
following: 

a)  Name  of  the  material; 

b)  Blend  composition   in   accordance   with  IS 
1793  :  1973; 

c)  Indication  of  the  source  of  mannfacture; 

d)  Month  and  year  of  manufacture;  and 

e)  Length  and  width  of  the  blankets. 

7  1.1  The  blankets  may  also  be  marked  with  the^ 
Standard  Mark. 

8  PACKING 

8.1  The  blankets  shall  be  packed  in  bales  in  con- 
formity with  the  procedure  laid  down  in  IS  741  t 
1971  or  by  the  method  given  m  7.2  if  specifically 
required  by  the  buyer. 

8.2  Fifteen  blankets  of  the  same  variety  shall  be- 
individually  folded  and  placed  one  over  the  other. 
The  folded  blankets  shaJl  be  wrapped  in  a  layer 
each  of  polyethylene  film,  kraft  paper  and  hessian 
(  305  g/ra''  )  in  such  a  way  that  hessian  forms  the: 
outermost  layer.  Each^  layer  shall  have  an  over- 
lap of  minimum  10  cm.  The  outermost  layer 
shall  be  suitably  sticbed  with  jute  twine  and  the 
package  made  secure  by  means  of  steeJstjips  or 
hoops  of  medium  grade.  The  gross  mass  of  the 
bale  shall  uormalfy  not  exceed  3^  kg.

9.1  Lot 

The  quantity  of  blanket  having  same  blend  com- 
position and  supplied  to  one  buyer  against  one 
despatch  note  shati  constitute  a  lot. 

9.2  Unless  otherwise  agreed  between  the  buyer 
and  the  seller,  the  number  of  pieces  to  be  selected 
at  random  shaH  be  in  accordance  with  col  1  and  2 
of  Table  4.  To  ensure  randomness  of  selection 
IS  4905  :  1968  may  be  used. 

9.3  The  conformity  of  a  lot  to  the  requirements  of 
the  standard,  shall  be  determined  on  the  basis  of 
the  testa  carried  out  on  the  sample  selected  from 
the  /ot  as  mdicated  in  Tab/e  5.

METHOD  FOR  DETERMINATION  OF  MASS  OF  BLANKETS 


B.1  DIMENSIONS 

B-I.l  Determine  the  dimensions  length  and  width^ 
(  L  and  H' )  of  blanket  in  centimetres  by  the 
method  given  in  JS  1954  :  1969. 

B-2  MASS 

B-2*t  Determine  the  mass  {  M ),   in   kg,   of  the 


blanket  after  conditioning  for  at  least  24  hours  ixa. 
the  standard  atmosphere  of  65  d:  2  percent  rela- 
tive humidity  and  27  ±  2''C  temperature. 

B-2,2  Calculate  the  mass  of  the  blanket  as  given 
below:

Standard  Mark 

The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  by  the  provisions  of  the  Stsreau  of  indkm 
Standards  Act,  1986  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made  thereunder.  The  Standard  Mark  on 
products  covered  by  an  Indian  Standard  conveys  the  assurance  that  tfacy  have  been  produced 
to  comply  with  the  requirements  of  that  standard  under  a  weJJ  defined  system  of  inspection* 
testing  and  quality  control  which  is  devised  and  supervised  by  BIS  and  operated  by  the 
producer.  Standard  marked  products  are  also  continuously  checked  by  BIS  fox  conformity 
to  that  standard  as  a  further  safeguard-  Details  of  conditions  under  which  a  licence  for  the 
use  of  the  Standard  Mark  may  be  granted  to  manufacturers  or  prod  utters  may  be  obtained 
from  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards. 


fiXS  is  a  ftatutory  itutitution  established  under  the  Bureau  of  Indkm  Standards  Act^  19B6  to  promote 
hannonious  development  of  the  activitiet  of  standardization,  marldng  aad  quality  ctrtification  of  foods 
and  attending  to  connected  matten  in  the  country.
